Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 48:

There are three issues (masa'il) in this.

The first: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Nor didst thou recite before it any scripture, nor didst thou transcribe it with thy right hand﴾. The pronoun in "qablihi" (before it) refers to the Scripture, which is the Qur'an revealed to Muhammad (ﷺ). That is, "And you, O Muhammad, did not used to read before it, nor did you frequent the People of the Book. Rather, We revealed it to you in the utmost degree of inimitability (i'jaz), containing the unseen matters and other things. Had you been one who reads a book and writes letters, ﴿the falsifiers would have had doubt﴾," meaning from among the People of the Book, and they would have had a basis for their doubt, and they would have said, "What we find in our books is that he is an unlettered one (ummi), who neither writes nor reads, and he is not like that." Mujahid said: "The People of the Book would find in their books that Muhammad (ﷺ) does not write and does not read, so this verse was revealed." Al-Nahhas said: it is a proof of his prophethood to the Quraysh, because he neither reads nor writes and does not mix with the People of the Book, and there were no People of the Book in Makkah, yet he brought them the reports of the prophets and the nations, and doubt and suspicion were removed.

The second: Al-Naqqash mentioned in his tafsir of this verse, from al-Sha'bi, that he said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) did not die until he had written." He also cited the hadith of Abu Kushah al-Saluli, whose content is that he (ﷺ) read a document belonging to Uyaynah ibn Hisn and informed them of its meaning. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: "All of this is weak, and the statement of al-Baji, may Allah have mercy on him, is among them." I say: It occurs in Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of al-Bara' regarding the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to Ali: "Write the condition between us: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. This is what Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, has agreed upon." The polytheists said to him: "If we knew that you are the Messenger of Allah, we would have followed you" (and in another narration, "we would have pledged allegiance to you"), "but write: Muhammad ibn Abdullah." So he ordered Ali to erase it. Ali said: "By Allah, I will not erase it" [[maha al-shay' yamhuhu wa yamhaahu mahwan wa mahyan: dhahaba atharuhu (he erased a thing; it removed its trace).]]. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Show me its place," so he showed him, and he erased it and wrote "Ibn Abdullah." Our scholars, may Allah be pleased with them, said: The apparent meaning of this is that he, peace be upon him, erased that word, which was "Messenger of Allah" (ﷺ), with his own hand, and wrote "Ibn Abdullah" in its place. Al-Bukhari narrated it more clearly than this. He said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took the document and wrote." He added in another route: "And he did not do well at writing." So a group said: this apparent meaning is admissible for him, and that he wrote with his own hand, among them al-Simnani and Abu Dharr [[al-Simnani is Abu 'Amr al-Filastini. Abu Dharr is 'Abdullah ibn Ahmad al-Harawi, and al-Baji is Abu al-Walid.]] and al-Baji, and they held that this does not detract from his being unlettered, nor does it contradict His saying: ﴿nor didst thou transcribe it with thy right hand﴾, nor His saying: ﴿We are an unlettered nation, we do not write nor do we reckon﴾. Rather they regarded it as an addition to his miracles and an reinforcement of his truthfulness and the soundness of his message, because he wrote without having learned writing and without engaging in its means; rather, Allah, exalted is He, caused movements to occur through his hand and pen, from which letters resulted that Ibn Abdullah understood when reading them. Thus it was a departure from custom, just as he, peace be upon him, knew the knowledge of the first and the last without learning or acquisition, so that was more eloquent as a miracle and greater in his virtues. The name "unlettered" does not leave him because of this, and for this reason the narrator who reported this situation said: "and he did not do well at writing." So the name "unlettered" remained for him even though he is said to have written.

Our shaykh Abu al-'Abbas Ahmad ibn 'Umar said: Many of the jurists (mutafaqqihah) of al-Andalus and elsewhere denied this and vehemently rejected it, and attributed its speaker to disbelief. That is evidence of the lack of rational sciences (al-'ulum al-nazariyyah) and of not pausing before declaring Muslims to be unbelievers, and they did not perceive that declaring a Muslim an unbeliever is like killing him, as came from him, peace be upon him, in the Sahih. Especially the accusation against one whom the people of his age testified to as having knowledge, merit and leadership. Moreover, the matter is not definitive; rather its basis is the apparent meanings of authentic solitary reports (akhbar ahad sahihah), except that reason does not render them impossible, and there is no definitive text in the Shari'ah that makes their occurrence impossible. I say: Some later scholars said: whoever says it is a miraculous sign, it is said to him: it would have been a sign that is not denied, were it not that it contradicts another sign, which is that he was unlettered and did not write. By his being unlettered among an unlettered nation, the proof was established, the deniers were silenced, and doubt was cut off. How then would Allah, exalted is He, free his hand so that he writes and that becomes a sign? The sign is rather that he does not write, and miracles cannot be impossible for some of them to repel others. The meaning of "he wrote" and "took the pen" is rather that he ordered one of his scribes to write with it, and among the scribes of revelation before him (ﷺ) there were twenty-six scribes.

The third: Qadi 'Iyad mentioned from Mu'awiyah that he used to write in the presence of the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said to him: "Throw down the inkwell, sharpen the pen, make the ba' upright, separate the sin, do not make the mim hollow, beautify the Allah, extend the Rahman, and perfect the Rahim." The Qadi said: Even if the report that he (ﷺ) wrote is not authentic, it is not far-fetched that he was granted knowledge of this and was prevented from reading and writing. I say: This is the correct view on the subject, that he did not write even a single letter, but rather he ordered one who would write; and likewise he did not read nor spell out letters. If it is said: The Prophet (ﷺ) did spell out letters when he mentioned the Dajjal and said: "Written between his eyes: k-f-r," and you say that the miracle subsists in his being unlettered, and Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Nor didst thou recite before it any scripture﴾ and the verse, and He said: ﴿We are an unlettered nation, we do not write nor do we reckon﴾, then how is this? The answer is what he (ﷺ) stated in the hadith of Huzayfah, and the hadith is like the Qur'an, one part of it explains another. In the hadith of Huzayfah: "Every believer, whether a writer or a non-writer, will read it," so he explicitly stated, regarding this matter, those who are unlettered other than the writers. And this is among the clearest of things that are evident.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 49:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Rather, it is clear signs﴾, meaning the Qur'an. Al-Hasan said: Al-Farra' claimed that in the reading of Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud), "Rather, they are clear signs" (bal hiya ayatun bayyinatun), the meaning is: rather, the signs of the Qur'an are clear signs. Al-Hasan said: Similar to it is ﴿This is insights﴾, and if this were the reading, it would be permissible; its parallel is ﴿This is a mercy from my Lord﴾. Al-Hasan said: This community was given memorization, whereas those before it did not read their scripture except by looking at it, and when they closed it, none of them retained what was in it except the prophets. Ka'b said, describing this community: They are wise scholars, and in understanding (fiqh) they are prophets.

(In the breasts of those who have been given knowledge), that is, this Qur'an is not as the falsifiers say, that it is sorcery or poetry, but it is signs and indicators by which the religion of God and His rulings are known. And it is thus in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge, namely the Companions of Muhammad (ﷺ) and the believers in him, who memorize it and recite it. He described them with knowledge because they distinguished, by their understanding, between the speech of God and the speech of humans and the devils. Qatadah and Ibn 'Abbas said: "Rather, He" meaning Muhammad (ﷺ), "is clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge" from among the People of the Book, who find him written with them in their books with this description: an unlettered one who neither reads nor writes; but they wronged themselves and concealed it. This is the choice of al-Tabari. The evidence for this view is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn al-Sumayqa: "Rather, this is clear signs." He (ﷺ) was signs, not a single sign, because he indicated many matters of the religion, so He said: "Rather, He is clear signs." It was also said: Rather, He is one possessing clear signs, and the noun was omitted.

(And none deny Our signs except the wrongdoers), that is, the disbelievers, because they denied his prophethood and what he brought.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 50–52:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they say, "Why were no signs sent down upon him from his Lord?"﴾ This is the statement of the polytheists to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and its meaning is: "Why was there not sent down upon him a sign like the signs of the prophets?" It is said: like the she-camel that Salih brought, and Musa's staff, and Isa's raising of the dead. That is, say (to them), O Muhammad: ﴿Signs are only with Allah﴾, so He brings them as He wills; when He wills, He sends them, and they are not in my hands. ﴿And I am only a plain warner.﴾ Ibn Kathir, Abu Bakr, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "āyah" in the singular. The rest read it in the plural. This is the preference of Abu 'Ubayd, because of His saying, may He be exalted: "Say: Signs are only with Allah."

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Is it not sufficient for them that We have sent down to you the Book, which is recited to them?﴾ This is a reply to their saying, "Why were no signs sent down upon him from his Lord?" That is: Is it not enough for the polytheists, among the signs, that this Book, which is miraculous, has been sent down, the Book with which you have challenged them to produce its like, or a single sura of it, and they were unable to do so? Even if you had brought them the signs of Musa and Isa, they would have said: "It is magic," and we do not know magic. Speech is within their capacity, yet despite that they were unable to produce a counterpart. It is said: the cause of the revelation of these verses is what Ibn 'Uyaynah related from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Yahya ibn Ja'dah, who said: A plate (kataf) with a writing on it was brought to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "Enough for a people to be misguided that they turn away from what their Prophet brought to what another prophet, other than their prophet, brought, or a book other than their book." Then Allah, may He be exalted, revealed: "Is it not sufficient for them that We have sent down to you the Book." Abu Muhammad al-Darimi related it in his Musnad, and the people of tafsir mentioned it in their books. In a similar vein, the Prophet (ﷺ) said to 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him): "Even if Musa ibn 'Imran were alive, he would have no choice but to follow me." And in a similar vein he (ﷺ) said: "He is not of us who does not chant the Qur'an" (yataghanna bil-Qur'an), meaning: who does not make himself independent through it of other things. This is al-Bukhari's (may Allah have mercy on him) interpretation of the verse. Since the reward for meeting one's Lord is ten good deeds for each letter or more, as we mentioned in the introduction of this book, turning away from it to something else is misguidance, loss, deception and deficiency.

(Indeed in that) that is, in the Qur'an, is ﴿surely a mercy﴾ in this world and the Hereafter. It is said: a mercy in this world through rescuing them from misguidance. ﴿And a reminder﴾ in this world, by guiding them through it to the truth, ﴿for a people who believe.﴾

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: "Allah suffices as a witness between me and you."﴾ That is: Say to those who deny you, "Allah suffices as a witness, who testifies for me to the truth of what I claim, that I am His Messenger, and that this Qur'an is His Book."

﴿He knows what is in the heavens and the earth﴾, that is, nothing is hidden from Him. This is an argument against them regarding the validity of His testimony over them, since they have acknowledged His knowledge, so it is binding upon them to acknowledge His testimony.

﴿And those who believe in falsehood﴾: Yahya ibn Sallam said: in Iblis. It is said: in the worship of idols and images, as stated by Ibn Shajarah.

﴿And disbelieve in Allah﴾, that is, through their denial of His messengers and their repudiation of His Book. It is said: through what they associated with Him of idols, and what they attributed to Him of children and equals.

﴿Those are the losers﴾: they lose themselves and their deeds in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 50–52:

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 53–55:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they ask you to hasten the punishment﴾. When he warned them of the punishment, they said, out of extreme denial: "Hasten for us this punishment." It was also said that the one who said this was al-Nadr ibn al-Harith and Abu Jahl, when they said: "O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then rain down on us stones from the sky" and their saying: "Our Lord, hasten for us our share (qittana) before the Day of Reckoning." And His saying: (And had it not been for a term appointed) concerning the descent of the punishment. Ibn 'Abbas said: it means what I promised you, that I would not punish your people and would delay them until the Day of Resurrection. Its explanation is: "Nay, the Hour is their appointed time." Al-Dahhak said: it is the duration of their lives in this world. It was said: what is meant by the appointed term is the first blast of the Trumpet; this was said by Yahya ibn Salam. It was said: it is the time that Allah decreed for their destruction and punishment; this was said by Ibn Shajara. It was said: it is the killing on the day of Badr. And in general, every punishment has a term that neither advances nor delays. Its proof is His saying: "For every news there is a fixed time (mustaqarr)."

(But the punishment would have come upon them): meaning the punishment they had asked to hasten.

(And it will come upon them suddenly): that is, unexpectedly.

(While they do not perceive): that is, they do not know of its descent upon them.

(They ask you to hasten the punishment): that is, they ask you to hasten it, though Hell has been prepared for them and it will surround them without doubt, so what is the meaning of seeking to hasten it? His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The Day the punishment will envelop them from above them﴾. It was said: this is connected to what precedes it, meaning: the Day the punishment will afflict them from above them and from beneath their feet; when the punishment envelops them, Hell will encompass them. I fed her straw and cold water [[the full line:

until the tears of her eyes flowed freely]]

And another said:

She was the leader of the horses toward the enemies, upon them a thicket of spears and coats of mail

**Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on Surah 29, verses 56–60**

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿O My servants who believe, indeed My earth is vast﴾

This verse was revealed to encourage the believers who were in Makkah to emigrate (hijrah). This is the view of Muqatil and al-Kalbi. Allah informed them of the vastness of His earth, and that remaining in one place under the harm of the disbelievers is not correct. Rather, the correct course is to seek the worship of Allah in His earth alongside His righteous servants. That is: if you are constrained from openly declaring faith (iman) in it, then emigrate to Madinah, for it is vast, so that you may proclaim monotheism (tawhid) there. Ibn Jubayr and Ata' said: the verse applies to any land in which injustice and wrongdoing are present, and emigration from it to a land of truth is obligatory. Malik also said this. Mujahid said: "Indeed My earth is vast" means: emigrate and strive (jihad). Mutarrif ibn al-Shikhkhir said: the meaning is that My mercy is vast. He also said: My provision for you is vast, so seek it in the earth. Sufyan al-Thawri said: "If you are in a land where prices are high, move to another land where you can fill your bag with bread for a dirham." It was also said: the meaning is that My earth, which is the earth of Paradise, is vast. "So worship Me" until I make you inherit it. "So worship Me" (fa-iyya-ya fa'budun): "iyya" is in the accusative governed by an implied verb, meaning: "so worship Me, worship Me," and one of the two verbs has been dispensed with in favour of the other. The fa' in His words "fa-iyya-ya" carries the sense of a condition, meaning: if a place is too confining for you, then worship Me elsewhere, because My earth is vast.

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Every soul shall taste death; then to Us you will be returned﴾

This has already been discussed in Al 'Imran [see vol. 4, p. 297 and following, first or second edition]. He mentions it here to belittle the affairs of this world and its frightening aspects. It is as if some of the believers considered the consequences that might befall them when leaving their homeland of Makkah, such as dying or going hungry or the like. So Allah belittled the worth of this world, meaning: you are certainly going to die and be gathered to Us. Therefore, hasten to the obedience of Allah, emigrate to Him, and to whatever brings about compliance with Him. Then He promised the believers who do righteous deeds dwelling in Paradise, as an exhortation from Him, and mentioned the reward they will receive. Then He described them with His words: ﴿Those who are patient and upon their Lord place their trust﴾.

Abu 'Amr, Ya'qub, al-Juhdari, Ibn Abi Ishaq, Ibn Muhaysin, al-A'mash, Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf recited "Ya 'ibadi" with a sukun on the ya'. The rest recited it with a fatha. Ibn 'Amir recited "inna ardi" with a fatha, and the rest with a sukun.

It is narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever flees with his religion from one land to another, even by a span of a cubit, deserves Paradise and will be the companion of Muhammad and Ibrahim, upon them both be peace."

His words: ﴿then to Us you will be returned﴾. As-Sulami and Abu Bakr, on the authority of 'Asim, recited "yurji'un" with a ya', in agreement with His words "every soul shall taste death". The rest recited it with a ta', in agreement with His words "O My servants who believe".

Some poets recited:

Death seeks out the shroud at every moment,
while we are heedless of what is intended for us.

Do not incline toward this world and its splendour,
even if you wrap yourself in its finest garments.

Where are the beloved ones and the neighbours, what have they done?
Where are those who used to be their dwelling place?

Death gave them a cup, not a pure one,
and placed them under the layers of the earth as pledges.

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will surely settle them in lofty chambers of Paradise﴾. Ibn Mas'ud, al-A'mash, Yahya ibn Wathhab, Hamza and al-Kisa'i recited "lanuthwiyannahum" with a tha' in place of the ba', from ath-thawy, which means to dwell, meaning: We will surely give them chambers in which they will dwell. Ruways, on the authority of Ya'qub, al-Juhdari and al-Sulami, recited "layubawwi'annahum" with a ya' in place of the nun. The rest recited "lanubawwi'annahum", meaning: We will surely lodge them. "Ghurafan" is the plural of ghurfah, which is an upper chamber that overlooks what is below.

In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Sahl ibn Sa'd [this is the narration of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, as in Sahih Muslim], the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the people of Paradise will look upon the people of the chambers above them as you look upon a bright star that is visible on the horizon, in the east or the west, because of the difference in their ranks." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, those are the dwellings of the prophets, which no one else can reach." He said: "Yes, by Him in whose hand is my soul, they are men who believed in Allah and affirmed the messengers."

Al-Tirmidhi related on the authority of Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed in Paradise there are chambers whose exteriors can be seen from their interiors and whose interiors can be seen from their exteriors." A Bedouin stood up and said: "For whom are they, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "They are for those who speak kindly, feed the hungry, fast continually, and pray at night while people are asleep."

We have explained this meaning further in the book "al-Tadhkirah", and all praise is due to Allah.

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿How many a creature there is that does not carry its provision; Allah provides for it and for you. And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾

Al-Wahidi related with a chain of narration through Yazid ibn Harun, who said: Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal narrated to us from al-Zuhri - he is 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Ata' - from 'Ata' from Ibn 'Umar, who said: We went out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) until he entered some of the orchards of the Ansar, and he began to pick dates and eat [and eat - this addition is from the book "Asbab al-Nuzul" by al-Wahidi]. He said: "O Ibn 'Umar, why do you not eat?" I said: "I have no desire for it, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "But I desire it, and this is the fourth morning that I have not tasted food. If I wished, I could ask my Lord and He would give me the like of the kingdom of Kisra and Caesar. So how will you be, O Ibn 'Umar, when you remain among a people who store up their provision for a year, and certainty weakens?" He said: "By Allah, we had not left until this was revealed: ﴿How many a creature there is that does not carry its provision; Allah provides for it and for you. And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾."

I say: This narration is weak, and what weakens it is that he (peace be upon him) used to store the year's provision for his family, as agreed upon by al-Bukhari and Muslim. The Companions also used to do this, and they were the exemplars, the people of certainty, and the leaders for those after them among the God-fearing who place their trust in Allah.

It is related that Ibn 'Abbas said that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to the believers in Makkah when the polytheists harmed them: "Go out to Madinah and emigrate, and do not dwell among the wrongdoers." They said: "We have no home there, no property, no one to feed us, and no one to give us drink." Then this was revealed: ﴿How many a creature there is that does not carry its provision; Allah provides for it and for you﴾, meaning: its provision is not stored with it. Likewise, Allah will provide for you in the abode of emigration. This is more fitting than the first view.

The discussion of "ka-ayyin" has already been mentioned: "ayyin" was preceded by the particle of comparison "ka", and it came to carry the meaning of "how many". According to al-Khalil and Sibawayh, the construction is understood as "like a number", meaning "like a great number of creatures".

Mujahid said: this refers to birds and beasts that eat with their mouths and carry nothing. Al-Hasan said: they eat at the time of need and do not store up for tomorrow. It was also said: "does not carry its provision" means it is unable to provide for itself. "Allah provides for it" wherever it turns, "and for you." It was also said that "carrying" here means "bearing responsibility" (hamalah). Al-Naqqash related that the intended reference is to the Prophet (ﷺ), who ate and did not store. I say: this is not correct, because the word "dabbah" (creature) is general, and in common usage it is not applied to a human being, so how could it be applied to the Prophet (ﷺ)? This has already been discussed in An-Naml, at His words: ﴿And when the word is fulfilled against them, We will bring forth for them a creature from the earth to speak to them﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "dawabb" refers to every living creature that crawls, and all of them do not carry their provision or store it, except for the son of Adam, the ant, and the mouse. Some of them said: "I saw the nightingale hoarding in its nest." It is said that the magpie has caches, but it forgets them.

"Allah provides for it and for you": He makes no distinction between the one who is greedy for provision and the one who trusts Allah for it, nor between the one who desires and the one who is content, nor between the strong and the weak, so that the strong man does not deceive himself into thinking he is provided for by his strength, and the weak man does not imagine that he is deprived because of his weakness.

In the Sahih, on the authority of the Prophet (ﷺ): "If you were to rely upon Allah with the reliance that is due to Him, He would provide for you as He provides for the birds: they go out hungry in the morning and return full in the evening."

(He is the All-Knowing) of your supplication and your saying: "We do not find anything to spend in Madinah," and of what is in your hearts.

Mujahid said: "Indeed My earth is vast" means: emigrate and strive (jihad). Mutarrif ibn al-Shikhkhir said: the meaning is that My mercy is vast. He also said: My provision for you is vast, so seek it in the earth. Sufyan al-Thawri said: "If you are in a land where prices are high, move to another land where you can fill your bag with bread for a dirham." It was also said: the meaning is that My earth, which is the earth of Paradise, is vast. "So worship Me" until I make you inherit it. "So worship Me" (fa-iyya-ya fa'budun): "iyya" is in the accusative governed by an implied verb, meaning: "so worship Me, worship Me," and one of the two verbs has been dispensed with in favour of the other. The fa' in His words "fa-iyya-ya" carries the sense of a condition, meaning: if a place is too confining for you, then worship Me elsewhere, because My earth is vast.

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Every soul shall taste death; then to Us you will be returned﴾

This has already been discussed in Al 'Imran [see vol. 4, p. 297 and following, first or second edition]. He mentions it here to belittle the affairs of this world and its frightening aspects. It is as if some of the believers considered the consequences that might befall them when leaving their homeland of Makkah, such as dying or going hungry or the like. So Allah belittled the worth of this world, meaning: you are certainly going to die and be gathered to Us. Therefore, hasten to the obedience of Allah, emigrate to Him, and to whatever brings about compliance with Him. Then He promised the believers who do righteous deeds dwelling in Paradise, as an exhortation from Him, and mentioned the reward they will receive. Then He described them with His words: ﴿Those who are patient and upon their Lord place their trust﴾.

Abu 'Amr, Ya'qub, al-Juhdari, Ibn Abi Ishaq, Ibn Muhaysin, al-A'mash, Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf recited "Ya 'ibadi" with a sukun on the ya'. The rest recited it with a fatha. Ibn 'Amir recited "inna ardi" with a fatha, and the rest with a sukun.

It is narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever flees with his religion from one land to another, even by a span of a cubit, deserves Paradise and will be the companion of Muhammad and Ibrahim, upon them both be peace."

His words: ﴿then to Us you will be returned﴾. As-Sulami and Abu Bakr, on the authority of 'Asim, recited "yurji'un" with a ya', in agreement with His words "every soul shall taste death". The rest recited it with a ta', in agreement with His words "O My servants who believe".

Some poets recited:

Death seeks out the shroud at every moment,
while we are heedless of what is intended for us.

Do not incline toward this world and its splendour,
even if you wrap yourself in its finest garments.

Where are the beloved ones and the neighbours, what have they done?
Where are those who used to be their dwelling place?

Death gave them a cup, not a pure one,
and placed them under the layers of the earth as pledges.

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will surely settle them in lofty chambers of Paradise﴾. Ibn Mas'ud, al-A'mash, Yahya ibn Wathhab, Hamza and al-Kisa'i recited "lanuthwiyannahum" with a tha' in place of the ba', from ath-thawy, which means to dwell, meaning: We will surely give them chambers in which they will dwell. Ruways, on the authority of Ya'qub, al-Juhdari and al-Sulami, recited "layubawwi'annahum" with a ya' in place of the nun. The rest recited "lanubawwi'annahum", meaning: We will surely lodge them. "Ghurafan" is the plural of ghurfah, which is an upper chamber that overlooks what is below.

In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Sahl ibn Sa'd [this is the narration of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, as in Sahih Muslim], the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the people of Paradise will look upon the people of the chambers above them as you look upon a bright star that is visible on the horizon, in the east or the west, because of the difference in their ranks." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, those are the dwellings of the prophets, which no one else can reach." He said: "Yes, by Him in whose hand is my soul, they are men who believed in Allah and affirmed the messengers."

Al-Tirmidhi related on the authority of Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed in Paradise there are chambers whose exteriors can be seen from their interiors and whose interiors can be seen from their exteriors." A Bedouin stood up and said: "For whom are they, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "They are for those who speak kindly, feed the hungry, fast continually, and pray at night while people are asleep."

We have explained this meaning further in the book "al-Tadhkirah", and all praise is due to Allah.

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿How many a creature there is that does not carry its provision; Allah provides for it and for you. And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾

Al-Wahidi related with a chain of narration through Yazid ibn Harun, who said: Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal narrated to us from al-Zuhri - he is 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Ata' - from 'Ata' from Ibn 'Umar, who said: We went out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) until he entered some of the orchards of the Ansar, and he began to pick dates and eat [and eat - this addition is from the book "Asbab al-Nuzul" by al-Wahidi]. He said: "O Ibn 'Umar, why do you not eat?" I said: "I have no desire for it, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "But I desire it, and this is the fourth morning that I have not tasted food. If I wished, I could ask my Lord and He would give me the like of the kingdom of Kisra and Caesar. So how will you be, O Ibn 'Umar, when you remain among a people who store up their provision for a year, and certainty weakens?" He said: "By Allah, we had not left until this was revealed: ﴿How many a creature there is that does not carry its provision; Allah provides for it and for you. And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾."

I say: This narration is weak, and what weakens it is that he (peace be upon him) used to store the year's provision for his family, as agreed upon by al-Bukhari and Muslim. The Companions also used to do this, and they were the exemplars, the people of certainty, and the leaders for those after them among the God-fearing who place their trust in Allah.

It is related that Ibn 'Abbas said that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to the believers in Makkah when the polytheists harmed them: "Go out to Madinah and emigrate, and do not dwell among the wrongdoers." They said: "We have no home there, no property, no one to feed us, and no one to give us drink." Then this was revealed: ﴿How many a creature there is that does not carry its provision; Allah provides for it and for you﴾, meaning: its provision is not stored with it. Likewise, Allah will provide for you in the abode of emigration. This is more fitting than the first view.

The discussion of "ka-ayyin" has already been mentioned: "ayyin" was preceded by the particle of comparison "ka", and it came to carry the meaning of "how many". According to al-Khalil and Sibawayh, the construction is understood as "like a number", meaning "like a great number of creatures".

Mujahid said: this refers to birds and beasts that eat with their mouths and carry nothing. Al-Hasan said: they eat at the time of need and do not store up for tomorrow. It was also said: "does not carry its provision" means it is unable to provide for itself. "Allah provides for it" wherever it turns, "and for you." It was also said that "carrying" here means "bearing responsibility" (hamalah). Al-Naqqash related that the intended reference is to the Prophet (ﷺ), who ate and did not store. I say: this is not correct, because the word "dabbah" (creature) is general, and in common usage it is not applied to a human being, so how could it be applied to the Prophet (ﷺ)? This has already been discussed in An-Naml, at His words: ﴿And when the word is fulfilled against them, We will bring forth for them a creature from the earth to speak to them﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "dawabb" refers to every living creature that crawls, and all of them do not carry their provision or store it, except for the son of Adam, the ant, and the mouse. Some of them said: "I saw the nightingale hoarding in its nest." It is said that the magpie has caches, but it forgets them.

"Allah provides for it and for you": He makes no distinction between the one who is greedy for provision and the one who trusts Allah for it, nor between the one who desires and the one who is content, nor between the strong and the weak, so that the strong man does not deceive himself into thinking he is provided for by his strength, and the weak man does not imagine that he is deprived because of his weakness.

In the Sahih, on the authority of the Prophet (ﷺ): "If you were to rely upon Allah with the reliance that is due to Him, He would provide for you as He provides for the birds: they go out hungry in the morning and return full in the evening."

(He is the All-Knowing) of your supplication and your saying: "We do not find anything to spend in Madinah," and of what is in your hearts.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 61–62:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?"﴾ [al-Ankabut 29:61], the verse. When the polytheists reproached the Muslims for their poverty and said, "If you were upon the truth, you would not be poor," and this was a deception, and there were poor people among the disbelievers as well, Allah dispelled this doubt. Likewise is the saying of one who said, "If we emigrate, we will not find anything to spend," meaning: since you acknowledge that Allah is the Creator of these things, how do you doubt regarding provision? He in whose hand is the bringing into being of all existing things is not incapable of providing for His servant. For this reason He connected it with His saying, exalted is He: "Allah expands provision for whomever He wills of His servants and restricts it for him" [al-Ankabut 29:62].

(﴿So how are they turned away?﴾) meaning: how do they disbelieve in My oneness and turn away from My worship?

(﴿Allah expands provision for whomever He wills﴾) meaning: the matter of provision does not vary by faith or disbelief; so expansion and restriction come from Him, and therefore one should not reproach another for poverty, for everything is by decree and destiny.

(﴿Indeed Allah is All-Knowing of everything﴾) of your conditions and affairs. It has been said: He is All-Knowing of what sets you right, whether restriction or expansion.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 63–64:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And if you asked them, "Who sends down water from the sky,"﴾ i.e., rain from the clouds.

(﴿and with it gives life to the earth after its death﴾) i.e., after its barrenness and the dearth of its people.

(﴿they will surely say, "Allah."﴾) i.e., so once you acknowledge that, why do you associate partners with Him and deny the Resurrection? And since He is capable of that, He is capable of enriching the believers; so it was repeated for emphasis.

(﴿Say, "Praise be to Allah."﴾) i.e., for the proofs and evidences of His power that He has made clear.

(﴿But most of them do not understand.﴾) i.e., they do not reflect upon these proofs. It was also said: "Praise be to Allah" is for their acknowledgment of this. And it was said: it is for the sending down of water and the giving of life to the earth.

(﴿And this worldly life is nothing but amusement and play.﴾) i.e., something by which one is diverted and amuses himself; that is, what Allah gives the rich of the world is nothing but something that dwindles and passes away, like a game which has no reality and no permanence. Some of them said: "If the world remains for you, you do not remain for it." And he recited:

The world comes to us with other than what it was, and new affairs arise after former ones.
The nights pass with gathering and separation, and stars rise in them and set.
Whoever thinks that the time's joy will last, that is an impossibility; joy does not endure.
May God pardon the one who makes his concern one, and is certain that the cycles turn.

I say: all of this concerns the affairs of this world: wealth, status, and clothing beyond what is necessary for the sustenance of life and strength for acts of obedience. As for what of it is for Allah, that belongs to the Hereafter, and it is what remains, as He said: ﴿And there remains the Face of your Lord, Full of Majesty and Honour.﴾ i.e., whatever is sought by it is its reward and His good pleasure.

(﴿And indeed the Last Abode, that is the true life.﴾) i.e., the abode of enduring life that does not pass away and in which there is no death. Abu 'Ubayda claimed that al-hayawan, al-hayat and al-hiyy (with a kasra on the ha') are one and the same, as the poet said [[The line is by al-'Ajjaj, and its completion is: "And when the time of people is dull"]]:

"And you see when life is hiyy"

Others said that hiyy is a plural formed on the pattern fi'wl, like 'isiyy. Al-hayawan applies to every living thing, and hayawan is also a spring in Paradise. It was also said: the root of hayawan is hayayan, then one of the two yas was changed into a waw because of the coming together of two like letters.

(﴿If only they knew.﴾) that it is so.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (*al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran*) on surah 29, verses 65–66:

Allah the Exalted's words: ﴿When they board the ship﴾ means the ships, and they fear drowning. (They call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion) means truthful in their intentions, and they abandon worshipping the idols and calling upon them.

(When He brings them safely to land, behold, they associate others with Him) means they call upon others alongside Him, and He did not send down any authority for it. It has been said: their association is that one of them says, "Were it not for Allah and the chief or the sailor, we would have drowned." Thus they make the deliverance that Allah granted them a share divided between Allah and His creation.

Allah the Exalted's words: ﴿So that they may deny what We have given them and so that they may enjoy themselves﴾. It has been said that both are *lam al-kay* (the lam of purpose), meaning: so that they may deny and so that they may enjoy. It has also been said that "behold, they associate others with Him" is for the purpose that the outcome of their association is that they deny the blessings of Allah and enjoy the world. It has also been said that both are *lam al-amr* (the imperative lam), meaning a threat and a warning: that is, deny what We have given you of blessing and deliverance from the sea, and enjoy yourselves. The evidence for this is the recitation (*qira'ah*) of Ubayy: "wa-tamatta'u" (and enjoy yourselves). Ibn al-Anbari said: this is reinforced by the recitation of al-A'mash, Nafi' and Hamzah: "wa-liyatamatta'u" with the lam pronounced with a jazm (sukun). Al-Nahhas said: "wa-liyatamatta'u" with a kasrah on the lam is *lam al-kay*, but it may also be *lam al-amr*, because the original form of *lam al-amr* is with a kasrah, except that it is an imperative carrying the meaning of threat. Whoever reads "wa-liyatamatta'u" with a sukun on the lam does not take it as *lam al-kay*, because the lam of purpose may not be given a sukun. This is the recitation of Ibn Kathir, al-Musayyibi, and Qalun from Nafi'; and Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, and Hafs from 'Asim; the rest read it with a kasrah on the lam. Abu al-'Aliyah recited: "li-yakfuru bima ataynahum fatamatta'u fasawfa ta'lamun", which is a threat and a warning.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 67–68:

Allah's words: ﴿Have they not seen that We made a sanctuary secure, while people are being snatched away from around them?﴾ ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: It is Makkah, and they are the Quraysh, whom Allah granted security therein. "While people are being snatched away from around them." Al-Dahhak said: some of them kill others and take others captive. Al-khatf (snatching) means taking swiftly. It has already passed in "al-Qasas" and elsewhere. So Allah, mighty and majestic, reminded them of this blessing so that they would submit to Him in obedience, meaning: I made for them a secure sanctuary in which they were safe from captivity, raids and killing, and I rescued them on land just as I rescued them at sea, yet they associate partners with Me on land and do not associate partners with Me at sea. This is an expression of wonder at the contradiction in their conditions.

﴿Then in falsehood do they believe?﴾ Qatadah said: then in shirk. Yahya ibn Sallam said: then in Iblis.

﴿And in the blessing of Allah do they disbelieve?﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: then in the well-being (ʿafiyah) of Allah. Ibn Shajarah said: then in the gift and favour of Allah. Ibn Sallam said: then in what the Prophet (ﷺ) brought of guidance. Al-Naqqash related: then in His feeding them after hunger and granting them safety after fear, do they disbelieve? This is an expression of wonder and denunciation, delivered in the form of a question.

Allah's words: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah or denies the truth when it has come to him?﴾ That is, there is no one more unjust than one who sets up with Allah a partner and a son, and when he commits an immoral act he says: "We found our fathers doing it, and Allah commanded us to do it."

(Or denies the truth when it has come to him.) Yahya ibn Sallam said: the Quran. Al-Suddi said: the Oneness (tawhid). Ibn Shajarah said: Muhammad (ﷺ). Every one of these statements encompasses both views.

﴿Is there not in Hell an abode for the disbelievers?﴾ That is, a dwelling-place (mustaqarr). This is a question seeking affirmation.

**Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on Surah 29, verse 69:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who strive for Us﴾, meaning, who strive against the disbelievers for Our sake, that is, seeking Our good pleasure. Al-Suddi and others said: this verse was revealed before the obligation of fighting (qital). Ibn 'Atiyyah said: it refers to the time before the customary jihad (al-jihad al-'urfi, jihad as an organized military campaign), and it is rather a general jihad in the religion of God and in seeking His good pleasure. Al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan said: the verse refers to the worshippers. Ibn 'Abbas and Ibrahim ibn Adham said: it refers to those who act upon what they know. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever acts upon what he knows, God will teach him what he does not know." Some scholars drew support from His saying: "Fear God, and God will teach you" (2:282). 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz said: "What has kept us from knowing what we do not know is our failure to act upon what we know. Had we acted upon some of what we know, it would have bequeathed us knowledge that our bodies could not bear." God, may He be exalted, said: "Fear God, and God will teach you." Abu Sulayman al-Darani said: the jihad in the verse is not only fighting the disbelievers, but is supporting the religion, refuting the falsifiers, subduing the wrongdoers, and, most important, commanding right and forbidding wrong. It also includes striving against the self (mujahadat al-nufus) in obedience to God, and this is the greater jihad. Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said to Ibn al-Mubarak: "When you see people disagreeing, then hold fast to the warriors (al-mujahidin) and the people of the frontiers (ahl al-thughur), for God, may He be exalted, says: ﴿We will surely guide them﴾." Al-Dahhak said: the meaning of the verse is, "And those who strive in emigration (al-hijrah), We will surely guide them to the paths of steadfastness in faith." Then he said: the example of the sunnah (the Prophetic way, the normative practice) in this world is like the example of Paradise in the Hereafter: whoever enters Paradise in the Hereafter is safe, and likewise whoever adheres to the sunnah in this world is safe. 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas said: "And those who strive in Our obedience, We will surely guide them to the paths of Our reward." This, by the generality of obedience, encompasses all sayings. Similar to this is the saying of 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: "Wisdom says: whoever seeks me and does not find me should seek me in two places: that he act upon the best of what he knows, and that he avoid the worst of what he knows." Al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl said: there is an inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in it, meaning: those whom We guided are those who strove for Us. ﴿We will surely guide them to Our paths﴾, that is, the way to Paradise, as al-Suddi said. Al-Naqqash said: He grants them success to the religion of truth. Yusuf ibn Asbat said: the meaning is, "We will surely purify their intentions, their charities, their prayers, and their fasting."

(﴿And indeed, God is with the good-doers﴾) The lam is a lam of emphasis (lam al-ta'kid), and it entered upon "ma'a" (with) in one of two ways. Either "ma'a" is a noun, and the lam of emphasis only enters upon nouns; or it is a particle, and the lam enters upon it, because it carries the sense of stability (al-istiqrar), just as you say: "Indeed, Zayd is surely in the house" (inna Zaydan la-fi al-dar). When "ma'a" is vowelled with a sukun, it is only a particle. When it is vowelled with a fathah, it may be either a noun or a particle, and most often it is a particle which comes for a meaning. The meaning of ihsan (goodness, excellence) and of the good-doers (al-muhsinin) was discussed in "al-Baqarah" and elsewhere. He, glory be to Him, is with them through support, assistance, protection and guidance; and He is with all creatures through encompassing knowledge and power. Thus there is a distinction between the two kinds of "with."

The Surah of al-'Ankabut is complete, and praise belongs to God alone. Completed with the help of God, the Exalted, is the thirteenth part of the Tafsir of al-Qurtubi, followed, God willing, by the fourteenth part, beginning with Surah al-Rum. The Fourteenth Part.
